title: Microsoft stops on Friday the 13th – level 3
paragraphs: A major global Microsoft outage on Friday the 13th disrupted essential services for hundreds of thousands of users worldwide and affected Outlook, Teams, Microsoft 365, OneDrive, and Copilot.

At the peak of the disruption, a monitoring website recorded over 130,000 reports for Outlook and 46,000 for Microsoft 365. Microsoft said a core process on its servers became overwhelmed and stopped responding, but ruled out a cyberattack and began a gradual recovery. A cybersecurity expert noted that the incident highlights the serious risks of businesses relying on a single technology provider for daily operations. When major cloud platforms fail, companies can lose access to emails, online meetings, and security verification codes, which brings daily work to a standstill.

Experts advise organizations not to put all their eggs in one basket, and urge them to diversify their digital providers and prepare strong backup plans to stay resilient during future technical crashes.
